comments.author: dlwh
comments.story: Ask HN: So what's new in the world of A.I.?
comments.text: As others have pointed out, a lot of things that "work" stop being considered AI. But here are a few recent advances off the top of my head: The DARPA Grand Challenge. Robot cars that drive themselves. [LINK] [VIDEO] Google's Machine Translation system. Far from perfect, but it can usually do something reasonable between over 40 different pairs of languages. They added Latin on Thursday. CMU researchers have developed a classifier that can look at your MRI scans and tell what you're thinking. (Still in its infancy, but still.) [LINK] People working in my research lab are working to automatically reconstruct words from the ProtoAustronesian language using just the modern words. Our results are typically extraordinarily close to what historical linguists have done by hand. People in a neighboring lab are working on a system that can automatically distinguish between a nuclear detonation and an earthquake as part of the Test Ban Treaty Organization. They're making good progress. Take a look at PhotoSynth: [LINK] which can automatically reconstruct 3D scenes from disparate photos taken from different cameras with no prior information needed to stitch them together. [LINK] The face detection that is now standard on many cameras was one of the great problems in computer vision.
